newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville lowers next-day peak-hour prices.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville lowers next-day peak-hour prices.

text.p: Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) Monday dropped its price offers for pre-scheduled power during heavy-load hours on Tuesday by $2.00 to $18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the agency said.
Bonneville also offered power during shoulder hours on Tuesday at $16.00 and during early morning low-demand hours at $13.00.
A volume limit of 800 megawatts was placed on pre-scheduled sales during hours ending 0600 and 2400 PDT.
Prices for Monday's schedulings had ranged from $13.00 per MWh for early morning hours to $20.00 for power between 1000 and 2000 PDT.

BPA had withdrawn from offering surplus power during peak-demand hours early last week following the expiration of extra dam flow requirements related to fish migration, but resumed those offers for Sunday and Monday.
Trade sources speculated that the federal power marketing agency lowered its prices to compete with other Northwest power suppliers.
